title: Create admin API endpoints in chatbot/api/admin.py
description:
Create chatbot/api/admin.py exposing a FastAPI APIRouter with endpoints for the admin dashboard: trace inspection, metrics summaries, structured log queries, and usage reports. All endpoints read from the in-memory TraceCollector, MetricsCollector, and StructuredLogger singletons.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/README.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/DISPATCH.md
- chatbot/observability/__init__.py (created by task t.1, updated by task t.2 — understand all exported symbols)
- chatbot/observability/tracing.py (created by task t.1 — TraceCollector and TraceRecord APIs)
- chatbot/observability/metrics.py (created by task t.2 — MetricsCollector and model metric APIs)
- chatbot/observability/logs.py (created by task t.2 — StructuredLogger and event query APIs)
- chatbot/api/__init__.py or existing API endpoint files for router pattern conventions

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/api/admin.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Create chatbot/api/admin.py with:
   - Module docstring: 'Admin dashboard API endpoints — trace inspection, metrics summaries, structured log queries, and usage reports.'
   - A FastAPI `APIRouter` instance named `admin_router` with prefix '/admin' and tag 'admin'.

2. Define Pydantic response models:
   - `TraceSummary`: trace_id (str), session_id (str), turn_id (str), model_id (str | None), task_class (str | None), total_latency_ms (float), prompt_tokens (int), completion_tokens (int), cost_usd_micros (int), created_at (str).
   - `TraceDetail`: all TraceRecord fields serialized (extends TraceSummary with prompt, routing_decision, retrieval_snippets, steps, retrieve_latency_ms).
   - `TraceListResponse`: traces (list[TraceSummary]), total (int), page (int), page_size (int).
   - `MetricsGlobal`: total_requests (int), total_tokens (int), total_cost_usd_micros (int), avg_latency_ms (float), models_used (int).
   - `ModelMetricSummary`: model_id (str), provider (str), request_count (int), total_prompt_tokens (int), total_completion_tokens (int), total_cost_usd_micros (int), avg_latency_ms (float), p50_latency_ms (float), p95_latency_ms (float), p99_latency_ms (float).
   - `ModelMetricsListResponse`: models (list[ModelMetricSummary]).
   - `LogEventResponse`: event_id (str), event_type (str), timestamp (str), session_id (str | None), turn_id (str | None), details (dict), severity (str).
   - `LogEventsListResponse`: events (list[LogEventResponse]), total (int).
   - `UsageReportResponse`: total_sessions (int), total_turns (int), total_tokens (int), total_cost_usd_micros (int), per_model (list[ModelMetricSummary]).

3. Endpoints:
   - GET '/traces': Accepts session_id (optional query param), page (int, default 1), page_size (int, default 50, max 200). Returns TraceListResponse.
   - GET '/traces/{trace_id}': Returns TraceDetail or 404.
   - GET '/metrics/global': Returns MetricsGlobal from metrics_collector.get_global_summary().
   - GET '/metrics/models': Returns ModelMetricsListResponse from metrics_collector.get_model_metrics_all().
   - GET '/logs': Accepts event_type (optional), session_id (optional), since (optional ISO timestamp), limit (int, default 100), offset (int, default 0). Returns LogEventsListResponse.
   - GET '/usage': Returns UsageReportResponse computed from metrics_collector.
   - GET '/health': Simple alive check returning {'status': 'ok', 'traces_stored': int, 'events_stored': int}.

4. All endpoints are read-only. No write operations. No auth dependency (admin endpoints are for operator use; auth is handled at router registration or via a future middleware). Wrap any internal errors in try/except returning 500 with a standard error message.
